title: Resolve, one recorded run
sop: KYB onboarding SOP (sop/kyb_sop.md), the approved spec spec/kyb-v1.json and the six example case files

steps.title: Z3 checks the SOP
steps.result: Z3 finds 3 problems in version 1 of the rules.
steps.text: Resolve runs Z3 on the rules in use today (version 1, approved) and works out each example case file's outcome from its facts. Z3 finds three problems in the SOP itself. Each one is found for every possible case, not just the six examples.

steps.title: Claude writes the questions
steps.result: Claude writes a question and two options for each problem.
steps.text: For each problem, Claude writes a question for the policy owner in plain words, two options, and the spec edit each option means. Claude only proposes: each edit must load and quote the SOP.

steps.title: Resolve shows what each option would change
steps.result: All 6 options are checked before the owner answers: 3 remove their problem, and 2 of those would raise a new one.
steps.text: Before the owner answers, Resolve applies each option's edit and runs Z3 again: does the problem go away, does the edit cause a new one, which kinds of case decide differently (with an example of each), and which past cases flip.

steps.title: The owner answers, and Resolve writes version 2 of the rules
steps.result: The two answers become version 2 of the rules. One example case now gets a different decision, and the change opens one new gap.
steps.text: An answer changes the rules, so Resolve never edits the rules in use: it writes the changes as a new version, and version 1 stays in force until the owner approves a replacement. Version 2 holds exactly the edits the owner was shown. Under it, Cedar Ridge Payments, a money services business with a verified licence, is approved instead of escalated. Z3 checks version 2 and finds one new gap: what to do while a licence check hasn't come back. Step 3 warned that this answer would open it.

steps.title: Claude asks about the new gap
steps.result: Claude asks the owner what to do while a licence check is still open.
steps.text: The new gap gets a question and two options, the same way as in step 2.

steps.title: Resolve shows what each option would change
steps.result: Waiting for the licence check closes the gap. Escalating now leaves the rules as they are.
steps.text: As in step 3, each option is checked against version 2 before the owner answers.

steps.title: The owner answers, and Resolve writes version 3
steps.result: One more answer gives version 3, and Z3 finds no problems left in it.
steps.text: Each round of answers makes a new version, so this second round gives version 3. Like version 2, it isn't in use until the owner approves it.

steps.title: The owner approves version 3
steps.result: The owner approves version 3, and it replaces version 1 as the rules in use.
steps.text: The approval is tied to the exact text the owner reviewed, so if version 3 changed afterwards the approval wouldn't count. Cedar Ridge's case file still says escalate because it was decided under version 1, so Resolve flags it to be run again under the new rules.
